priorBlockers.evidence: The witness was that git diff 57d55ac...HEAD -- infra/ returned zero files. It now returns eight. infra/terraform/modules/app/main.tf:150-197 creates aws_ssm_parameter.signwell_api_key and .signwell_webhook_secret as SecureStrings with lifecycle.ignore_changes on value and a placeholder, never a real value; iam.tf:68-72 adds both ARNs to the execution-role ssm:GetParameters document unconditionally; api.tf adds SIGNWELL_API_APPLICATION_ID, SIGNWELL_TEST_MODE and PROVIDER_SYNC_STALE_SECONDS to locals.api_environment and gates the two secret ARNs on var.signwell_secrets_provisioned; the dead SIGNATURE_PROVIDER entry is gone. Both tfvars carry the flag false with the put-parameter commands, and docs/deployment.md now holds the four go-live steps and why a placeholder is never handed to the container.

applySignature is awaited at apps/api/src/signing/signing.service.ts:340; the transaction opens at :361 and takes its FOR UPDATE at :365. No provider port method runs between the lock and the commit, which is invariant 11 and acceptance criterion 12.

createDocument now takes the lookup as a required second parameter (signwell-http-client.ts:54-57). HttpSignWellClient.attempt consults it after the backoff whenever the failure being retried could have been processed: couldHaveLanded is true on a transport error (:424) and on a 5xx (:412) and explicitly false on a 429 (:405), and the hook runs at :383 before the next request. A found document is thrown out of the loop as AdoptedExisting and returned by createDocument (:209-228), so a create that may have landed is never repeated. createOrAdopt passes the scan in (signwell-signing-provider.ts:204) and keeps the post-exhaustion scan for the fifth attempt (:215). The test the witness asked for exists: apps/api/test/signwell-client.spec.ts:151-221 drives a timeout and asserts exactly one POST /documents, one lookup and one backoff; asserts the create is still repeated when the lookup finds nothing; and asserts no lookup is spent on a 429.

findings.claim: Carried from review 1 (N1) and still open, though the code has answered half of it. Requirement 24a says any read of a non-terminal envelope triggers a synchronous re-fetch; only EnvelopesService.get at :414 and SigningService.view at :127 call convergeIfStale. The list deliberately does not, and the reason is now written at envelopes.service.ts:341-356 - but it is written in the code, while CLAUDE.md says the spec is what changes when behaviour and spec disagree. A note rather than a blocker because the spec's own acceptance of 24a is envelope-level: TC-04-INT-11 and TC-04-INT-12 both exercise GET /envelopes/{id}, and the alt flow at spec:930 says the next read of the envelope. So any read is loose prose, not a rule the implementation fails.

witness.detail: Requirement 24a: Any read of a non-terminal envelope whose providerKey is remote and whose providerSyncedAt is older than PROVIDER_SYNC_STALE_SECONDS (default 120) triggers a synchronous re-fetch before the response is composed. Applied literally to the list, one page of up to a hundred rows would spend up to a hundred provider calls, serialized per organization under a 10s deadline each, against the 120-per-minute read budget requirement 19 pins - which is why the code refuses, and why the sentence rather than the code is what should move.

findings.suggestedFix: One sentence in requirement 24a: any read of a single non-terminal envelope - the detail read and the signing page, never the list, which would spend one call per row against the budget requirement 19 names.

findings.rule: specs/documents/04-signature-providers.md - requirement 38 and the Error Messages table
findings.claim: Carried from review 1 (N4) and review 2 (N2), unchanged by e1cece1. A text-tag materialization failure is reported to the sender with the provider-unavailable copy - Signing service is unavailable, nothing was sent, try again shortly - but a retry fails identically, because the tags will not parse on the next attempt either. The machine-readable code and the expected and received lists are right; only the sentence is wrong, and the spec supplies no other.

witness.detail: Requirement 38: On mismatch the send deletes the document, leaves the envelope in draft, and reports document_fields_not_materialized naming what was expected and what came back. The Error Messages table at spec:1067-1089 has no row for that case, so the only string available to the handler is SIGNING_PROVIDER_MESSAGES.send.providerUnavailable.

findings.suggestedFix: Add a row to the Error Messages table for document_fields_not_materialized and put the string in packages/validation beside the others.

findings.claim: The vendor iframe is given allow=camera; microphone; clipboard-write on /sign/{token}, the one session-less page in the product. Nothing in the spec asks for it: the Blast Radius row about this page's policy widens frame-src only and says outright that script-src is deliberately untouched, and requirement 15's whole argument is that no third-party capability is spent to save a postMessage handler. Granting camera and microphone to the embed origin is a capability of exactly that kind, and it is recorded nowhere.

witness.detail: Blast Radius, The CSP on /sign/*: frame-src gains the embed origin and nothing else, from a build-time variable. script-src is deliberately untouched: requirement 15 hosts the widget in our own iframe with our own origin-checked listener rather than loading SignWell's SDK, so no third-party script reaches that page. The iframe attribute grants the frame two device capabilities the same reasoning would not have granted a script.

findings.suggestedFix: Drop the allow attribute unless the widget genuinely needs a camera for identity capture; if it does, record that in requirement 15 beside the frame-src decision so the grant is a decision rather than a default.

findings.claim: provider_error is added to EnvelopeEventType, to the Prisma enum and to the migration, and nothing ever writes it: the reconciler records failure on Envelope.providerError at provider-reconciler.service.ts:508-513 and writes only provider_synced events. The Data Model does ask for both values, so the code matches the spec - recorded so nobody reads the enum as evidence that provider failures reach the audit trail.

witness.detail: Spec Data Model: EnvelopeEventType gains provider_synced, provider_error. Grepping provider_error across apps and packages returns only the enum declaration, the generated dist copy and the TC-02-UNIT-02 assertion - no writer.

findings.suggestedFix: Either write a provider_error event where recordProviderError runs, or say in the Data Model row that the value is reserved and unused this release.

findings.claim: The per-organization serialization map is never pruned: this.queues gains one entry per organization id that ever sends and keeps it, holding a settled promise, for the life of the process. Small and slow, and no rule forbids it, but the API is long-lived and this is the only unbounded map in the client.

witness.detail: serialize() calls this.queues.set(key, next.then(...)) on every request and there is no delete anywhere in the file.

findings.suggestedFix: Delete the entry in the settled continuation when it is still the current one for that key.
